result.reason: The closed FCSTM's root/initial pseudostate enters only the synthetic UnspecifiedInitial leaf (transition:line:17, [*] -> UnspecifiedInitial), which has no outgoing transitions (LEAF_WITHOUT_OUTGOING/W_DEADLOCK_LEAF). None of the six authored operating states (DoorShut, DoorOpen, DoorOpenWithItem, DoorShutWithItem, ReadytoCook, Cooking) are reachable_from_initial (all false per inspection_equivalent_facts.states and verify_facts reachability checks, all status=refuted). This single root cause explains why every transition_endpoints contract's source state is unreachable and why every declared event has zero reachable consumers (EVENT_CONSUMER_UNREACHABLE for Cancel, Door_Opened, Item_Removed, Item_Placed, Door_Closed, Cooking_Time_Entered, Start, Timer_Expired). Per frontier discipline, a present exact endpoint transition is not itself a wrong-target/dead-end violation merely because its source is unreachable; the correct behavioral-consequence obligations are: (1) the NL1-INIT-1 initial_entry contract itself, which is directly violated since root/system does not enter DoorShut but a synthetic placeholder instead (S2 candidate on the owner-local initial edge, target mismatch: required DoorShut vs actual UnspecifiedInitial); and (2) one derived reachability contract for the DoorShut operating scope, since without reaching DoorShut none of the door/microwave behavior described in NL1-NL8 can ever execute, which is a distinct global reachability defect from the local initial-edge target mismatch. I also derive one event_consumer_coverage contract at the whole-machine scope because every declared event's consumer set is uniformly unreachable, which is a single systemic coverage gap traceable to the same root unreachability rather than eight independent per-event violations; I aggregate all declared event/consumer refs in one contract's basis instead of emitting one candidate per event, consistent with 'aggregate supporting consumer refs in basis rather than emitting one issue per transition.' I did not derive separate deadlock_freedom candidates for the six authored states because each has exact outgoing transitions in the closed model (only unreachable, not dead-ended), consistent with 'an unreachable state that has exact outgoing continuation is not a deadlock/dead-end violation.' I omit per-endpoint wrong-target candidates for the individual transition_endpoints contracts (NL1-ENDPOINT-1 through NL8-ENDPOINT-*, NL1-DERIVED, NL4-DERIVED) because their exact source/target/trigger pairs are all present and correctly wired in the closed transition inventory (tr_0001..tr_0015 map 1:1 to transitions line18..line32); the only defect is upstream reachability, captured in the derived contracts, not a per-transition wrong_target defect. branches.reason: The closed FCSTM's root/initial pseudostate enters only the synthetic UnspecifiedInitial leaf (transition:line:17, [*] -> UnspecifiedInitial), which has no outgoing transitions (LEAF_WITHOUT_OUTGOING/W_DEADLOCK_LEAF). None of the six authored operating states (DoorShut, DoorOpen, DoorOpenWithItem, DoorShutWithItem, ReadytoCook, Cooking) are reachable_from_initial (all false per inspection_equivalent_facts.states and verify_facts reachability checks, all status=refuted). This single root cause explains why every transition_endpoints contract's source state is unreachable and why every declared event has zero reachable consumers (EVENT_CONSUMER_UNREACHABLE for Cancel, Door_Opened, Item_Removed, Item_Placed, Door_Closed, Cooking_Time_Entered, Start, Timer_Expired). Per frontier discipline, a present exact endpoint transition is not itself a wrong-target/dead-end violation merely because its source is unreachable; the correct behavioral-consequence obligations are: (1) the NL1-INIT-1 initial_entry contract itself, which is directly violated since root/system does not enter DoorShut but a synthetic placeholder instead (S2 candidate on the owner-local initial edge, target mismatch: required DoorShut vs actual UnspecifiedInitial); and (2) one derived reachability contract for the DoorShut operating scope, since without reaching DoorShut none of the door/microwave behavior described in NL1-NL8 can ever execute, which is a distinct global reachability defect from the local initial-edge target mismatch. I also derive one event_consumer_coverage contract at the whole-machine scope because every declared event's consumer set is uniformly unreachable, which is a single systemic coverage gap traceable to the same root unreachability rather than eight independent per-event violations; I aggregate all declared event/consumer refs in one contract's basis instead of emitting one candidate per event, consistent with 'aggregate supporting consumer refs in basis rather than emitting one issue per transition.' I did not derive separate deadlock_freedom candidates for the six authored states because each has exact outgoing transitions in the closed model (only unreachable, not dead-ended), consistent with 'an unreachable state that has exact outgoing continuation is not a deadlock/dead-end violation.' I omit per-endpoint wrong-target candidates for the individual transition_endpoints contracts (NL1-ENDPOINT-1 through NL8-ENDPOINT-*, NL1-DERIVED, NL4-DERIVED) because their exact source/target/trigger pairs are all present and correctly wired in the closed transition inventory (tr_0001..tr_0015 map 1:1 to transitions line18..line32); the only defect is upstream reachability, captured in the derived contracts, not a per-transition wrong_target defect. I likewise omit per-transition guard/effect/action candidates that are satisfied at the structural level (this lens defers those specific carrier-field judgments to the structure-contrast lens; behavior_consequence focuses on reachability/consumption/termination). For NL6-ENDPOINT-1/NL8-ENDPOINT-3 (Cancel returning to ReadytoCook/DoorShutWithItem) and other cyclic returns, no stable-termination contract is supplied (this model has no designated termination_state), so no termination candidate applies.
